quote.text: In every walk with nature, one receives far more than he seeks.
quote.author: John Muir

fun_fact.text: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards! They can also hover in mid-air by flapping their wings in a figure-eight pattern up to 80 times per second. These tiny acrobats have the highest metabolism of all animals and must eat about half their body weight in sugar daily.

short_read.title: The Secret Lives of Seals in the Salish Sea
short_read.teaser: Harbor seals and their larger cousins, elephant seals, are year-round residents of the waters around Port Angeles. Learn about their playful personalities and surprising intelligence.

medium_read.title: The Lost Art of Hungarian Embroidery
medium_read.teaser: Hungarian embroidery traditions date back centuries, with each region developing its own distinctive patterns and colors. This beautiful craft is experiencing a renaissance as younger generations rediscover their heritage.

long_read.title: Olympic National Park: A Journey Through Three Ecosystems
long_read.teaser: From alpine peaks to temperate rainforests to wild Pacific coastline, Olympic National Park contains three distinct ecosystems within its boundaries. Discover the incredible diversity right in Barbara's backyard.

port_angeles.title: Black-Tailed Deer at Hurricane Ridge
port_angeles.description: August is a wonderful time to spot black-tailed deer and their fawns grazing in the meadows at Hurricane Ridge. The deer are most active in early morning and evening, often approaching visitors with gentle curiosity. They're unique to the Pacific Northwest and smaller than their white-tailed cousins.

puzzle_1.question: A hummingbird's heart beats approximately ___ times per minute while in flight.
puzzle_1.correct_response: That's exactly right, Barbara! Their tiny hearts beat incredibly fast to fuel their amazing flying abilities.
puzzle_1.close_response: You're very close! Their hearts beat about 1,200 times per minute — that's 20 times per second!
puzzle_1.wrong_response: Their hearts actually beat about 1,200 times per minute! That's what it takes to power those incredible wings.
puzzle_1.learn_more_text: To put this in perspective, a human heart beats about 60-100 times per minute at rest. Hummingbirds need this rapid heartbeat to deliver oxygen to their wing muscles during their energy-intensive hovering flight.

puzzle_2.question: Which Hungarian word means 'butterfly'?
puzzle_2.correct_response: Wonderful, Barbara! Pillangó is such a beautiful word for such a beautiful creature!
puzzle_2.wrong_response: The word is 'pillangó' — doesn't it sound lovely? (Madár means bird, virág means flower, and méhecske means little bee.)
puzzle_2.learn_more_text: The Hungarian word 'pillangó' is thought to come from an old word meaning 'to flutter.' Hungary is home to over 200 species of butterflies, including the beautiful swallowtail.

puzzle_3.question: What unique feature helps sea otters stay in one place while they sleep?
options: They anchor to rocks with their tails
They hold hands or wrap themselves in kelp
puzzle_3.correct_response: Yes! Sea otters often hold hands with each other or wrap themselves in kelp to keep from drifting apart while sleeping. It's one of nature's sweetest sights!
puzzle_3.wrong_response: Sea otters actually hold hands with each other or wrap themselves in kelp! This keeps them from drifting away from their group while they rest.
puzzle_3.learn_more_text: Sea otters in the waters around Port Angeles form groups called rafts, sometimes numbering over 100 individuals. They spend most of their lives in the water and have the densest fur of any animal.
